Hi Simon — thanks for the clear note and the AP matrix. Quick summary and options below so your AP team can pick what they prefer.

Option A (preferred for simplicity): You send the full gross EUR amount to our EUR collection account. Redwood will absorb any intermediary/correspondent fees and credit your USD payout as per agreed FX rules. We would then invoice the gross amount and Redwood bears the cost of any third-party intermediary charges.

Option B (net collection): You send funds but instruct your bank to debit any correspondent charges and send net amount. Redwood will accept net receipts; however final USD credit will be lower and we will annotate the remittance with the net received amount. This requires the payer to accept variability on the received amount.

Operational notes:
- For Option A we need a short instruction in the invoice that the payer must NOT mark "sender pays" for beneficiary bank charges (we can provide phrasing).
- For Option B please ensure your bank includes MT103 trace data and the beneficiary reference so we can map fees.

I've looped in Vanessa (sales) and Laura (finance) — Vanessa: pricing decision? Laura/Marissa: can payments ops provide the exact collection account wording and the SWIFT narrative we should ask Borealis to use?

I'll wait for your preference and will send the invoice template with the chosen instruction.

Best,

Thanks — operational inputs from Finance / Payments:

1) Recommended invoice wording (for Option A):
"Please remit gross EUR amount to: [Redwood EUR Collection Account - IBAN: XX...]. Redwood will absorb reasonable correspondent bank fees up to EUR 150 per invoice. Any fees above EUR 150 will be recharged to the payer upon reconciliation. Please include invoice number and MT103 trace in remittance details."

2) SWIFT narrative suggestion to reduce hops:
- Field 70 (Remittance Information): INV RWF-2028-1273
- Field 59 (Beneficiary): REDWOOD INFERENCE LTD / IBAN XX...
- Field 72 (Sender to Receiver Information): /OUR (if your bank supports) — but DO NOT instruct "SHA" or "BEN" as those can force different routing. Note: /OUR may increase payer bank charges so confirm via AP.

3) VAT and tax handling:
- Since the invoice is EUR to an EU entity, apply standard VAT rules (reverse charge if customer is VAT-registered and provides valid VAT ID). We'll include a VAT note on the invoice template and request Borealis' VAT ID.
- For any USD payout and FX gain/loss, Redwood will treat realized FX differences in line with our finance policy; these are not customer-billable outside of explicit pass-through items.

4) Reconciliation ask: please provide MT103 or SWIFT copy for any payment where net received differs from invoice by > EUR 10 so we can attribute intermediary fees.

I've attached a brief bank instruction stub and a proposed fee split table for your records. Marissa — Payments Ops: please confirm the EUR collection account and whether we can accept MT202/103 trace mapping for faster identification.

Laura Bennett
